inositol phospholipid breakdown, via phospholipase C, is the mechanism by which bradykinin exerts its biological actions on NG115‐401 cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bradykinin‐induced Ca2+ signal in NG115‐4011 cells is mediated via a receptor‐coupled GTP‐binding protein which stimulates the production of inosiol 1,4‐5‐tris‐phosphate and in turn the release of Ca2+.

the bradykinin receptors on the NG115‐401l cells are coupled to phosphatidylinositol hydrolysis, and that inositol trisphosphate is likely to be the second messenger coupling receptor stimulation to Ca2+ release from intracellular stores.
bradykinin stimulates a rapid increase in inositol phospholipid breakdown, with the initial production of inosito‐1,4, 5‐tris phosphate, inositol tetraphosphate and inosiol bisphosphate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inositol trisphosphates are not only involved in Ca2+ release from internal stores but also in Ca2+ uptake and sequestration into internal stores.
bradykinin is a powerful stimulator of phosphoinositide metabolism in NG115‐4011 cells.
